sections.label: IMF roles and funding sources
sections.summary: The IMF performs economic surveillance, lending and capacity development, funded mainly by members' quotas supplemented by borrowing arrangements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The IMF performs three main roles in furtherance of its mission: first, economic surveillance; second, lending to member countries; and third, capacity development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The primary and permanent source of the IMF's funds is members' quotas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Quota resources are supplemented by multilateral borrowing arrangements with member countries which are in a stronger financial position, such as the New Arrangements to Borrow (NAB) and Bilateral Borrowing Agreements (BBAs).

sections.label: Bill amends BWAA repayment requirement
sections.summary: The Bill amends BWAA to waive early repayment where the agreement is in IMF's standard form or cannot be suspended.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Bill will, thus, amend BWAA to waive the early repayment requirement in instances where: (a) the relevant agreement is in a standard form provided by IMF, which MAS cannot amend unilaterally; or (b) the relevant agreement is for an IMF arrangement or programme which cannot be suspended or prematurely terminated.

sections.label: Singapore's loan exposure to IMF
sections.summary: Singapore's loan exposure is to IMF, IMF loans are repaid ahead of other creditors, and IMF must repay immediately if Singapore has a balance of payments need.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: That is, Singapore's loan exposure is to IMF, not borrowing countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: This means that loans granted by IMF will be repaid ahead of all other creditors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Third, as I mentioned earlier, should Singapore have a balance of payments need, IMF is already obliged under our loan agreements to repay the loan to Singapore immediately.

sections.label: MAS subscription to Singapore's quota share
sections.summary: Section 4 of BWAA empowers MAS to subscribe to Singapore's quota share of SDR 3.9 billion, about US$5.5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Next, section 4 of BWAA empowers MAS to subscribe to Singapore's quota share which is currently Special Drawing Rights (SDR) of 3.9 billion amounting to about US$5.5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: If it is funded, what is the interest rate and can we sell the SDR back to IMF in the event Singapore needs funds urgently?

sections.label: Grant to Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust
sections.summary: The agreement allows Singapore to provide a US$20 million grant to the Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust, which provides loans to low-income countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The agreement allows Singapore to provide a US$20 million grant to the Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust (PRGT) which provides loans to low‐income countries.

sections.label: Largest allocation in institution's history
sections.summary: The amount came up to 465 billion SDRs, or US$650 billion, the largest in the institution's history.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The amount came up to 465 billion SDRs, or US$650 billion, the largest in the institution's history.

sections.label: Singapore SDR allocation versus reallocation
sections.summary: Singapore received 3.7 billion new SDRs, or $2.8 billion, in the 2021 general allocation, over one hundred times more than it re-allocated.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, for the 2021 general allocation, Singapore received 3.7 billion new SDRs, which works out to $2.8 billion dollars.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Put another way, what we chose to re-allocate was more than one hundred times less than the amount we received in new SDR allocations that year.

sections.label: Development is not zero-sum
sections.summary: Development is not a zero-sum game, so lower-income countries receiving financial support do not cause other countries to fall behind.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One of the magical benefits of development is that it is decidedly not a zero-sum game.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, when today's lower-income countries receive financial support that enables them to vault into the next stage of their development journey, their improved incomes are not coming at the expense of any other country necessarily falling behind.

sections.label: Foreign aid and goodwill
sections.summary: Singapore's economy has largely recovered from COVID-19 while many others report GDP below pre-pandemic levels, and providing timely aid can garner goodwill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Singapore's economy has largely recovered from COVID-19, but many others are still facing the repercussions of the shock and are reporting GDP figures below their pre-pandemic levels.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given how timely such support will be, we can also garner an immense amount of intangible goodwill by becoming a more active provider of foreign aid.

sections.label: Singapore's World Bank loans history
sections.summary: Singapore received 14 World Bank loans between 1963 and 1975, repaid them by the mid-1980s, and is now more likely to provide assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As we started out as a developing nation, we benefited from no less than 14 loans from the World Bank between 1963 and 1975 to build our water, port, sewage, power and telecommunications infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: These loans were repaid by the mid-1980s and, today, Singapore is a developed country which is more likely to provide, rather than receive, assistance through the World Bank and IMF.

sections.label: MAS overseas offices cost
sections.summary: The question asks how much MAS has cost to sustain the operations and functions of these offices in each of the last five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How much has it cost MAS to sustain the operations and functions of these offices in each of the last five years?

sections.label: IMF RST lending facility
sections.summary: The IMF created the RST in April 2022 to provide affordable long-term financing to low-income and vulnerable middle-income countries for macro-economic policy reforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: On lending, IMF created a new lending facility, the RST, which Assoc Prof Lim talked about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: They did so in April 2022 to provide affordable, long-term financing to low-income and vulnerable middle-income member countries in support of macro-economic policy reforms related to structural challenges, including climate change.

sections.label: Singapore IMF loan commitments
sections.summary: Since the 2016 BWAA amendment, Singapore committed US$1.9 billion under the NAB and US$1.7 billion under the BBA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Since the BWAA was amended in 2016, Singapore has made loan commitments of US$1.9 billion to IMF under the NAB for 2021 to 2025 and US$1.7 billion under the BBA for 2021 to 2024.

sections.label: Grants to IMF trust funds
sections.summary: Three grants are proposed: US$17.6 million to the CCRT, US$2 million to the COVID-19 capacity initiative, and US$0.97 million to the poverty trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: First, an additional grant of US$17.6 million to the IMF's CCRT; second, a grant of US$2 million to the IMF's COVID-19 Crisis Capacity Development Initiative, which seeks to meet the urgent capacity development needs of countries affected by the COVID-19 pandemic; and three, a grant of US$0.97 million to the IMF's Trust for Special Poverty Reduction and Growth Operations for Heavily Indebted Poor Countries.

sections.label: MAS funding for IMF offices
sections.summary: Between FY2019 and FY2022, MAS provided an annual average of about $2.3 million to the STI and $390,000 to the RRO.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In terms of the quantum of financing that has been provided to the IMF offices in Singapore, between financial year (FY) 2019 and FY2022, MAS provided an average of about $2.3 million to the STI annually and about $390,000 to the RRO annually.

sections.label: IMF loan repayment safeguards
sections.summary: IMF has preferred creditor status and must repay Singapore immediately if Singapore has a balance of payments need, with early repayment provisions required.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Second, as IMF enjoys preferred creditor status, loans granted by IMF must be repaid ahead of all other creditors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Third, should Singapore have a balance of payments need, IMF is obliged under our loan agreements to repay the loan to Singapore immediately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I emphasise that where the IMF arrangement or programme can be prematurely terminated or suspended, and where the terms of any agreements for loans or financial assistance can be unilaterally amended, MAS will require IMF to include an early repayment provision in accordance with BWAA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I want to assure him and emphasise that MAS will continue to exercise a high degree of prudence when considering each IMF request for financial assistance.
